headline: Recommended renaming the committee Public Outreach & Communications Committee, and discussed fall outreach and strategic plan feedback.
summary: The committee gave early feedback on the draft strategic plan and reviewed summer tabling results. It planned fall outreach and deferred choosing the December article topic to October. It agreed to recommend a new committee name to Governance.
decisions: Approved the July 16, 2026 meeting minutes with minor edits, passed unanimously.
Agreed to recommend Public Outreach & Communications Committee as the committee's new name to Governance.
Deferred choosing the topic for the December article to the October meeting.

plain_text:
LIBRARY BOARD OF TRUSTEES COMMUNICATIONS COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES – 9.17.26 
 
 
DRAFT MINUTES 
LIBRARY BOARD OF TRUSTEES 
COMMUNICATIONS COMMITTEE MEETING 
September 17, 2026  
 
The committee held a regular meeting on September 17, 2026 at 5:30 p.m. in the SBPL 
Board Room, and by Zoom. 
 
Members present: Holly Painter, Chair; Whitney Kirzinger, Rebecca Stazi, Leslie Van 
Wagner 
 
Not present: Bree Drapa, Library Director; Stacey Pape 
 
1. Call to order (5:35 p.m.) Chair Holly P. called the meeting to order at 5:35 p.m. A sign-in 
sheet for the Chair and Committee members was shared to mark their meeting 
attendance.  
 
2. Review of library exits Chair provided instructions on emergency building exits.  
 
3. Additions and deletions to the posted agenda Committee name discussion 
 
4. Comments and questions from the public not related to items on the agenda No 
public present 
 
5. Approval of regular committee minutes of July 16, 2026 
MOTION: Rebecca S. motioned to approve the July 16, 2026 meeting minutes with minor 
edits. SECOND: Leslie V. ACTION: Motion passed unanimously.  
6. Strategic plan & staff communications survey  
• As a member of the Library’s Strategic Plan working group, Whitney S. invited the 
Communications Committee members to provide early/directional feedback on the draft 
strategic plan, particularly Goal 3: Community Awareness and Engagement and its 
objectives as it most clearly relates to marketing and communications efforts. 
• Strategic Planning Committee: Incorporate committee feedback before the draft goes to 
the Board on October 8. 
• Staff communications survey: Use the survey findings to help inform future initiatives 
under the strategic-plan objectives, particularly outreach to 
underserved/underrepresented audiences. 
• Flag for further refinement: 
o Consider whether the word “cultural” should be included in the description of the 
library as a trusted civic, cultural and community resource.
LIBRARY BOARD OF TRUSTEES COMMUNICATIONS COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES – 9.17.26 
 
o Make the objectives around the library as a trusted community resource and a 
community support partner more distinct. 
o Consider how advocacy/support for library resources, staffing and funding fits 
within Organizational Alignment & Capacity. 
• Follow up on strategic-plan implementation: Clarify how annual initiatives will be 
developed by library staff and how the committee will have visibility into and support 
those initiatives. 
7. Summer Tabling/Pride debrief 
Summer tabling takeaways: 
• Interactive activities generated more engagement than simply handing out materials. 
• Pete the Cat was particularly effective at attracting people. 
• For future events, incorporate more hands-on/interactive activities, such as: 
o Library of Things items for people to explore 
o Art activities 
o Kids' activities 
o Special guests/read-alouds or collaborations with other community organizations 
• Continue looking for opportunities to piggyback on existing community events, but begin 
planning the summer outreach schedule earlier in the spring. 
• School events were worthwhile and generated library-card/sign-up interest, but stronger 
signage/branding is needed when the library is participating without a tent. 
• Continue using branded tablecloths/T-shirts and consider additional simple signage 
identifying the library. 
• Explore having a library staff member present at events when possible, particularly when 
library cards or other staff-only services can be offered on site. 
8. Fall outreach 
8.a. Tabling (schools, Al’s, new Rec opportunities) 
• Clarify with Bree which upcoming Recreation Department/community events already 
have library staff attending and where trustees/committee members are being asked 
to provide additional support. 
• Add the October, November and December opportunities to the outreach 
spreadsheet and circulate them to the full Board of Trustees for volunteer sign-ups. 
• Do not include September events in the current volunteer request as the time is too 
short to secure sign-ups. 
• Pace participation realistically given current library staffing constraints; the Committee 
should be choiceful about covering every opportunity.
LIBRARY BOARD OF TRUSTEES COMMUNICATIONS COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES – 9.17.26 
 
• Prioritize events where: 
• Library staff will already be present. 
• Library cards or other library services can be offered. 
• The event reaches audiences beyond people who already regularly engage with 
the library. 
Explore additional outreach opportunities with: 
• South Burlington Food Shelf 
• Apartment communities 
• Local businesses 
• Lowe’s / Home Depot / Panera or similar community-oriented businesses 
• Recreation Department events, including hockey/open skate opportunities 
• Other areas of South Burlington identified as having fewer library-card holders 
Holly to talk with Bree about the Food Shelf opportunity and determine whether/when the library 
could participate. If so, Rebecca will reach out to the Director of the Food Shelf. 
Holly to talk with Sue about outreach locations and audiences she believes the library should 
prioritize. For example, follow up with the apartment-management company regarding outreach 
at the apartment communities previously identified. 
Consider using the library’s community/library-card data map to help identify areas and 
audiences with lower library participation and target outreach accordingly. 
8.b. December article for The Other Paper 
The Communications Committee is responsible for the December article which would be due 
around the first week of December. We will defer topic selection until the October meeting. 
Before selecting a topic, check with Bree regarding what they plan to highlight in January and 
whether there are strategic priorities or recent statistics that would make a strong December 
story. Possible direction discussed: highlighting library growth and increased community use, 
using recent statistics such as library-card growth and increased utilization. 
8.c. Other Ideas? 
The Committee members brainstormed and discussed other ideas including: 
Continue developing outreach beyond the committee’s traditional “same audience” events. 
Explore unexpected/nontraditional community locations where library outreach could reach 
people who may not already be connected to the library.
LIBRARY BOARD OF TRUSTEES COMMUNICATIONS COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES – 9.17.26 
 
Consider partnerships with local businesses and community organizations as a low-cost way to 
increase library visibility. 
Explore opportunities to distribute library information/materials at community businesses and 
gathering places. 
Continue thinking about how to make outreach interactive and memorable, rather than simply 
informational. 
Other business 
The Committee agreed that Public Outreach & Communications Committee is the preferred 
direction/name to recommend to Governance. Holly will notify Governance of the committee’s 
preference. The current name remains Communications Committee until the bylaws are formally 
changed. 
The Committee members agreed to continue discussing/defining the committee’s role and scope 
to avoid mission creep and clarify the distinction between trustee-led public outreach and library 
staff communications/PR. 
Adjourn The meeting was adjourned at 6:58 p.m. 
 
 
 
 
 
Respectfully submitted,   
Rebecca Stazi
